1.d4 Nc6 2.c4 e5 3.d5 Nce7.strategy: Steps back to a flexible square, from which the knight eyes the d5-pawn and can go to g6. Black concedes space for a compact position with a strong e5 pawn, and prepares to attack White's centre with a pawn break in a closed game.
1.d4 Nc6 2.c4 e5 3.d5 Nce7.name: Bogoljubov–Mikenas Defence: Lithuanian Variation

1.d4 Nc6 2.c4 e5 3.d5 Nd4.strategy: Centralises the knight on a square protected by the e5-pawn. But White can drive it away with e3 and gain a tempo, and the knight has little future there, so Black risks falling behind in development against White's space edge.
1.d4 Nc6 2.c4 e5 3.d5 Nd4.name: Bogoljubov–Mikenas Defence: Cannstatter Variation
